memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'The rest of the grain offering belongs to Aaron and his sons; it is a most holy part of the food offerings presented to the LORD.'" - Lev 2:3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The larger part of the grain offering did not burn. It fed the priests.

This was practical. The tribe of Levi received no land in Canaan (Num 18:20). They had no fields, no harvest of their own. God's arrangement was that His servants would be sustained by the offerings of His people. When an Israelite brought fine flour, a priest's family ate that day.

So worship and provision were woven together. The Israelite's gift to God became bread on another believer's table. Paul saw the same principle still operating in the church: those who preach the gospel should receive their living from the gospel (1 Cor 9:14). And in Philippians he called the church's financial gift to him a fragrant offering, an acceptable sacrifice, pleasing to God (Phil 4:18) — reaching back to this exact language.

Notice too the phrase most holy. The priest's meal was not a leftover or a perk. It was set apart, treated with reverence.

There is a quiet lesson here about how we regard those who serve us spiritually, and about how those who serve should regard what they receive. Both sides are holy ground.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I see supporting God's work as a genuine act of worship, or merely as an expense?
2. Who has served me spiritually that I could thank or support this month?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that You provide for Your servants through Your people. Make me generous, and make me grateful for those who feed me from Your Word. Amen.
